messages.subject: better facet labelling
parts:
I would like to rotate the text of my facet labels so they are horizontal, and I would like a better way to do the labelling.

<example>
library("ggplot2")
vote <- data.frame(State=c("OH", "MO"), Clinton=c(0.470, 0.428), k=seq(2))

flabel <- function(variable, value) {
if (is.factor(value))
return(value)
vote$State[value]
}

ggplot(vote, aes(x=Clinton, y=0.1))+facet_grid(k~., labeller=flabel) +
geom_point()+scale_x_continuous(formatter="percent")
</example>

Naturally I would prefer to use State directly as a facet, but I also want to control the sort order. Also, I've had trouble with some plots using State as the y value.

The web has advice, most notably https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/ggplot2/hJI7bcX_rMk, but unfortunately the commands aren't available in my version (0.8.9) and I haven't found anything similar that works. For example,
ggplot(vote, aes(x=Clinton, y=0.1))+facet_grid(k~., labeller=flabel) +
theme_text(angle=90)+geom_point()+scale_x_continuous(formatter="percent")
Error: Don't know how to add theme_text(angle = 90) to a plot
